clue.text: Evil lunatic raves? Just the opposite

parts.note: vice is wickedness, a synonym for evil

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters of raves are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a madman's rantings as meaning the reverse of what they say.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Just the opposite' look like a reply to the ravings; that reply is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used to say the reverse relation also holds, the other way round.

clue.text: Left part of book that is very lacking, initially

indicators.note: lacking its first letter, so the opening letter of the phrase for very is dropped

parts.note: ever so is an informal way of saying very

explanation.surface: A book's left-hand section is judged badly deficient from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very' is EVER SO; 'lacking, initially' drops its first letter E. 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, the left-hand page of an open book is called the reverse side, opposite the recto.

clue.text: Together they rally business with clubs

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
drivers are golf clubs used for long tee shots

explanation.surface: A firm's staff go out together with their golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: A rally is a motor race on public roads where a navigator sits beside the driver; both share the task.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people sharing driving duties in a motor rally are each called a co-driver.

clue.text: Without being asked, say, reworked novel? True

indicators.note: reworked means made over again, so the letters of novel and true are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader wonders whether a revised novel is now a true story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworked' rearranges NOVEL plus TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer information is to offer it freely, saying something unprompted.

clue.text: As users, authors get revised reference work

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters of users, authors and get are rearranged

explanation.surface: Writers, as well as ordinary readers, get an updated reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges USERS, AUTHORS and GET; 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous English book of synonyms, a standard reference work.

clue.text: They must accept charge added to an account for this treatment

indicators.note: added to says the following piece is joined after the account

parts.note: a version is someone's account of events

indicators.note: must accept means the word they takes another piece inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap

explanation.surface: Patients must accept a fee added to their bill for this treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a psychological treatment pairing an unwanted habit with something unpleasant to make it repellent.

clue.text: Have to interrupt enjoyment in bed

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so to goes inside the word for enjoyment

parts.note: fun is enjoyment

explanation.surface: Someone complains that having to do something spoils their fun in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese-style mattress laid on the floor or a low frame serves as a bed.

clue.text: Place to discuss ideas in class outside university

indicators.note: outside means the word for class is placed around the letter for university

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: A seminar room outside the university is somewhere to talk about ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts FORM around U.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman forum was a public square for debate; now any setting for open discussion.

clue.text: Do a dance from the 60s

definitions.meaning: to do someone is to swindle or cheat them
a rock and roll dance craze of the early 1960s, made famous by Chubby Checker

explanation.walkthrough: 'Do a dance' reads as one instruction, but 'Do' is a definition on its own, meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: cheating someone, and a gyrating dance popular in the sixties.

clue.text: Moving air heading towards the top of the charts

definitions.meaning: a wind is moving air, here one named after its compass direction

definitions.text: heading towards the top of the charts
definitions.meaning: maps and charts put north at the top, so this means going north

explanation.walkthrough: 'top of the charts' suggests a hit record, but these charts are maps.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a wind from the north and also describes a course pointed northward.

clue.text: Warning from editor following line in newspaper

indicators.note: in says the editor, following and line pieces sit inside the newspaper word

parts.note: rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: An editor issues a warning after spotting a line printed in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like an order word, but it is the abbreviation used in page references.
explanation.definitionFit: A red flag is a signal of danger, so a warning sign of trouble ahead.

clue.text: One intervening between noble and monarch in the past

indicators.note: intervening between means coming in the middle, so the letter for one sits between the two pieces

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone once stood between a nobleman and the monarch in times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, so it describes something that happened before now.

clue.text: Cause of tears, one understood by expert

definitions.meaning: chopping this vegetable makes the eyes water
an expert is said to know their ..., so this is what an expert knows

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition rests on the British idiom 'to know your onions', meaning to be expert in a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulb vegetable stings the eyes when cut, and features in an idiom about expertise.

clue.text: International affair put marriage under strain?

indicators.note: under in an across clue means the marriage piece comes after the strain piece

parts.note: a test is a strain or trial
a match is a marriage, as in a good match

explanation.surface: A diplomatic affair puts a couple's marriage under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket fixture between national sides, which is why 'International' alone can define it.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and rugby, a Test is a full international game between two countries.

clue.text: Bishop, for one, that is put in power by church

indicators.note: put in means the abbreviation for that is goes inside the other letters

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
CE is the Church of England
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A bishop is put into power by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clergy; the bishop is a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess bishop is one of the playing pieces on the board, so it is an example.

clue.text: American university's publicity included English college

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
inc. is short for included or including
Eton College is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: An American university's promotional material features an English college.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an elite boarding school near Windsor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Ivy League institution in New Jersey is a well-known American university.

clue.text: Decade of investment that was disastrous for Paris

definitions.text: Decade of investment that was disastrous for Paris

parts.words: Decade of investment that was disastrous for Paris
parts.note: investment is a siege; the Greeks besieged Troy for ten years, and Paris, the Trojan prince, died in it

explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' sounds financial and 'Paris' French, but this is the legendary ten-year siege of Troy, started when Paris took Helen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greeks besieged Troy for ten years after Paris abducted Helen, and he was killed in the fighting.

clue.text: Moral philosopher, as a parent, smacked hard

parts.note: Adam, the first man, is a parent of humankind
smit is an old past tense of smite, to strike
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A philosopher of morals, in his role as father, gave a child a hard smack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; SMIT is an archaic form of smote.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish economist wrote The Theory of Moral Sentiments and held a chair of moral philosophy.

clue.text: Drunken lot, we hear, in this drinking place

indicators.note: drunken means unsteady, so the letters of lot we hear stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunken crowd is overheard in this bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges LOT WE HEAR. 'we hear' looks like a sound signal, but it is fodder; 'in this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool where animals come to drink, and jokingly a pub, is a drinking place.

clue.text: Poles asking for quick response after current's rising

indicators.note: after says the poles and response pieces follow the current piece

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
N and S are the north and south poles
urgent means demanding immediate attention

explanation.surface: Polish people want a fast reply after the current situation escalates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests Polish people, but it is N and S. 'rising' is the definition, as in rising in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in revolt against authority is rebelling, as in an uprising.

clue.text: Suitably cast, finally, in adapted play

indicators.note: in places that final letter inside the rearranged play
adapted means changed, so the letters of play are rearranged
finally points to the last letter of the word cast

explanation.surface: An adapted play has been well cast, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes T from 'cast'; 'adapted' rearranges PLAY to APLY, and 'in' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Done aptly means done fittingly or appropriately, which is to act suitably.

clue.text: Type of government in state I quietly despise

parts.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for California, a US state
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
to hate is to despise

explanation.surface: Someone names a type of government in their state that they quietly despise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule by a caliph, a successor to Muhammad, was a form of Islamic government.

clue.text: Nobody's child left down and out? Not so, not so!

parts.words: down and out? Not so, not so
parts.note: each not so asks for the opposite word: not down gives up, not out gives in

explanation.surface: An orphan left penniless and homeless protests that it is not like that at all.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British comic novel The Diary of a Nobody, Lupin Pooter is the son of Charles Pooter. 'down and out' looks like destitution.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Grossmiths' novel The Diary of a Nobody, the narrator Pooter's son is so named.

clue.text: Ruth, without husband, in short

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for compassion surrounds the letter for husband

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or compassion

explanation.surface: Ruth, missing her husband, gets a brief mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a name, but it is the old noun for pity; 'without' means outside, the opposite of its surface sense. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithy writing is brief and to the point, so concise and short.

clue.text: Right to infiltrate fraudulent scheme to beat it

indicators.note: to infiltrate means to get inside, so R slips inside the word for a con

parts.note: a scam is a fraudulent scheme

explanation.surface: A right-winger infiltrates a fraud to defeat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat it' looks like defeating the scheme, but it is slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal commands to leave at once, as in clear off.

clue.text: What's rewritten by me, including article, perhaps

indicators.note: including means the rearranged letters hold the article inside
rewritten means written out differently, so the letters of by me are rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer asks what text they have revised, including an article, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges BY ME to MYBE, and 'including' puts A inside. 'What's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps are interchangeable adverbs expressing possibility.

clue.text: Supposed expert on horses from one end to another? Not quite

parts.note: a tip is an end, as of a finger

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: another end is the stern, the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A racing pundit's advice runs from one extreme to the other but falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the final N of STERN. 'Supposed' is the setter's dig at racing tipsters.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing tipster sells predictions about which horses will win, claiming expertise.

clue.text: Car included in any financial support

indicators.note: included in means the car word is placed inside the word any

parts.note: a limo, short for limousine, is a car

explanation.surface: A car is part of any package of financial support.
explanation.definitionFit: Maintenance paid to a former spouse after divorce is financial support.

clue.text: Local in Gotham?

parts.note: Gotham is the English village whose people were famed in folklore as fools, so a resident is a simpleton

explanation.walkthrough: Gotham suggests Batman's city, but the original is a Nottinghamshire village in English folklore whose inhabitants pretended to be foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninny is a fool, and the wise men of Gotham were famous fools.

clue.text: With which one raises a beam, about to snap

definitions.text: With which one raises a beam, about to snap

parts.words: With which one raises a beam, about to snap
parts.note: a beam is a broad smile, and to snap is to take a photograph; this is what a photographer says to prompt smiles

explanation.walkthrough: 'raises a beam' and 'snap' suggest a timber about to break, but beam is a grin and snap a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers use this phrase to make subjects smile just before the shutter clicks.
